newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine government outlines 1997 economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine government outlines 1997 economic plan.

text.p: The Ukrainian government has set as its main task the revival of production, still in decline five years after independence, the Economy Ministry said in unveiling the government's 1997 plan.

"This programme clearly shows that in the near future, state resources will be directed to achieving growth in the internal economy and deepening economic reforms," Vasyl Hureyev told Reuters. "This programme is more concrete and tougher than any previous government programme."
The programme, outlining objectives for the coming year, will be presented to parliament in accordance with Ukraine's first post-Soviet constitution passed in June.
All indicators set down in the plan match those in the 1997 draft budget submitted to parliament last week.
The budget calls for a 1.7-percent rise in gross domestic product (GDP) from this year. In the first half of 1996, the economy shrank 8.7 percent after contracting 11.8 percent in 1995.
The budget forecasts 24.9 percent inflation for 1997, nearly half of this year's projected rate, and a deficit at two percent of GDP by Western calculations.
Hureyev said the government would implement tough bankruptcy legislation and for the first time in the post-Soviet era, close down loss-making factories.
The programme also calls for privatising large factories and stresses what Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko and other ministers admit are protectionist measures to boost domestic production.
Hureyev also pledged to bring its shadow economy under control, estimated to account for 40 percent of the country's economic activity. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
